symptom: The documented second-tool procedure checked out the checkpoint tag and then validated, which reported CHECKPOINT_INVALID with a branch mismatch even though the commit was correct.

title: A control over a checkpoint's own evidence must be scoped to the moment it matters
symptom: The gate that validates the checkpoint kept failing because running it appends to the very ledger and inventory the validation binds.
rootCauseSummary: Consistency rules written for a finished delivery were applied while the delivery was still writing its own evidence, which no ordering of steps can satisfy.
resolution: Gate consistency is strict at handoff and provisional while work is in progress; every in-progress validation procedure uses the checkpoint-owned harness to declare append-only evidence dirty and re-derive hashes through finalize_checkpoint.refresh_declared_hashes immediately before validation. Self-observing process checks exclude their complete observer ancestry before classifying a matching process. Pre-finalization RUN-METADATA retains a valid RFC 3339 observation timestamp and HEAD; the finalizer alone replaces that timestamp with the true terminal boundary and writes final status and final commit immediately before the content commit. Direct validate_checkpoint.py is the post-finalization clean-boundary command, not the append-only in-progress runner. CP0010 adds guarded, unsealed-only derived metadata synchronization; evidence producers must finish before inventory declaration and validation. The checkpoint wrapper must not write a cached pre-synchronization STATE after the canonical producer has replaced it.

title: Two representations of one concept in one module disagree, and the safer one loses
symptom: redact_text redacted the committed example environment file's placeholders while redact_value left them alone. Reading a redacted example cannot answer the one question it is read for: whether a real value has leaked into it.
rootCauseSummary: The module defined what a placeholder looks like twice: once anchored, for values under a sensitive key, and once as a negative lookahead inside the text pattern. The two definitions were written at different times and disagreed about the repository's own documented placeholder. A comment noting that they must agree is not a mechanism that makes them agree.
resolution: The lookahead was removed. The text redactor now tests the matched value against the single anchored definition and leaves a placeholder in place, so there is one authoritative statement of what a placeholder is.

prevention.description: The placeholder the repository documents survives both redactors.

Every value in the committed example file is classified identically by both redaction paths. Its first run found a second instance of the same failure: an operational limit named ...MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS was redacted by one path only.
No module outside the redaction package decides for itself whether a name carries a credential.
Redaction and committability are different questions, and the difference is asserted rather than assumed.

applicability.requiredCheck: Where this Gate defines a classification twice — once anchored and once embedded — confirm one definition is authoritative and the other derives from it or is removed.

notes: Found only because GATE 1 rebuilt the image the gate measures; it had been red behind a green gate for a whole Gate (LSN-0036). The residual limit is that the scan recognises the shape the three offenders had; a rule expressed differently would pass it.

title: A test that writes to the operational database leaves production data behind
symptom: The first live catalog synchronisation returned 36 models from the provider and the catalog endpoint reported 56. Twenty rows belonged to providers named devworld-<hex> carrying models called model-one, keep and drop: fixtures from the integration suite, sitting in the operator-visible catalog and rendered by the web page.
rootCauseSummary: The store tests run against the stack's real database on purpose — that is what makes them prove the stores work against the real schema — and they created rows without removing them. Each run added another provider, its models and a model_calls row. Nothing was wrong with the product; the tests were writing production data.
resolution: An async scope context manager gives each test a unique provider slug and unique request identifiers and removes every row it created in a finally block, in foreign-key order. The residue already in the database was purged. A standing invariant now asserts that the catalog holds no provider the policy does not declare, so residue is detected rather than trusted not to appear.

prevention.description: Every provider row traces to .iacode/policies/providers.json.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every test this Gate adds that writes to a shared service rather than to a disposable one, confirm it removes what it created and that an invariant detects residue.
applicability.requiredEvidence: The suite run followed by a query of the shared service showing no fixture rows.

notes: A disposable database is the right tool for schema questions and the wrong one for store behaviour against the installation's own schema. The answer is cleanup, not a second database.

title: A control that judges sealed history only runs once a successor anchors it
symptom: MIR-016 failed with GATE-0-CP-0001: CHECKPOINT_INVALID. Six of that sealed checkpoint's recorded commands name var/verify-report.json as an input; var/ is ignored by Git, so no checkout of the tag carries it, and the validator required every declared input to exist.
rootCauseSummary: Two causes in one failure. The recorder declared a generated, ignored artifact as a command input, which makes the record unreplayable from a checkout. And the defect was invisible for a whole Gate because a checkpoint cannot anchor its own tag: GATE-0-CP-0001 entered the anchor chain only when its successor built the chain, so the first execution of the control over it happened one Gate after the content it judges was sealed.
resolution: The command-input policy is now versioned. Schema 3.3.0 requires every declared input to be eligible for Git transport, using one shared classifier that rejects Git metadata, ignored output, absolute paths and repository escapes. Automatic discovery excludes local-only paths, explicit inputs are refused before execution, and checkpoint validation independently rejects manually constructed records. Schemas through 3.2.0 retain digest-bound compatibility for sealed generated inputs, so current tooling can audit immutable predecessors without treating their local archives as new evidence.

prevention.description: Every anchored checkpoint validates from a detached checkout of its tag, asserted by the suite rather than only by the mirror audit.
A generated artifact is never recorded as a command input.
The rule still refuses a reference that resolves to nothing.

Every commit a checkpoint's evidence names must be reachable from a published reference (a branch, a tag or a remote-tracking branch); an object that exists only in the local store is refused, for every schema version (ADR-0028).

A record naming a commit no published reference reaches is refused, as a local object in the repository that holds it and as an absent object in a published clone; the same record passes once a published reference reaches the commit.
On the real sealed history, removing each refs/tags/iacode-preserved/ reference makes the checkpoint that names its commit invalid in the repository and in a published clone.
A published clone does not carry an unreachable object that a copy of the object store does.
A syntax-tree scan refuses any git clone in the tooling or the suite that is not a transport clone.
remote_sync.py refuses a local preserved or checkpoint tag that is not on the remote.
Every preserved commit is associated only with a checkpoint whose canonical command evidence fields name it; a SHA appearing merely in an argument cannot capture the guardrail's subject.
Git metadata is classified as local-only even though git check-ignore does not report it.
The strict schema refuses a content-bound .git input.
Local presence cannot make an ignored artifact transportable.
Auto-detection omits Git metadata and explicit declaration is rejected.
A recorded refusal is accepted only while the shared classifier reproduces it.
A fabricated refusal over a repository-carried input is rejected.
command_input_transport_error is the shared transport classifier.

applicability.requiredCheck: Confirm that every sealed predecessor this Gate anchors validates from a detached checkout of its own tag in a published clone (Git's transport, never a copy of the local object store), that every commit sealed evidence names is reachable from a published reference, and that no command this Gate records declares an input the repository does not carry.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A validation run against each anchored checkpoint from its tag in a published clone, green, and a clone of the remote that validates every sealed checkpoint of the milestone.

guardrailFailures.detail: GUARDRAIL_FAILURE: M1-F-003 (GATE-3-CP-0002): GATE-1-CP-0001 validates from its own tag in the working repository and not from the published history, because its sealed record cmd-0086 names commit b59d66f9f3f9, a replaced closure commit no published reference reaches. GRD-0042 stayed green because test_every_sealed_checkpoint_validates_from_its_own_tag cloned the local path with --no-hardlinks, which copies unreachable objects; MIR-016 cloned the same way. The control could not tell a local object from a published one.

GUARDRAIL_FAILURE: GATE-3-CP-0005 preserved-checkpoint association: GUARDRAIL_FAILURE: GATE-3-CP-0005 anchored GATE-3-CP-0003, whose tag-creation command mentions the preserved SETUP-00 commit only as an argument. GRD-0042's load-bearing-reference test selected a checkpoint by raw SHA substring, associated the commit with GATE-3-CP-0003 instead of SETUP-00-CP-0009, and therefore expected the wrong checkpoint to fail. The Git property and validator were correct; the guardrail could no longer identify its subject.

GUARDRAIL_FAILURE: G4-F-003: GATE-4-CP-0006 passed local sealing and publication checks while COMMANDS.jsonl cmd-0061 declared .git/gate4-cp0006-pre-red-retry.zip as an input. Git transport cannot carry repository metadata, but the recorder/validator classification relied on git check-ignore and local presence, so GRD-0042 stayed green until the canonical tag was validated from the remote.

notes: The residual limit remains honest: a pre-3.3 sealed checkpoint may carry only the digest of a generated input, not the input itself. Current tooling can classify and audit that legacy record, but only a successor checkpoint can provide new repository-carried evidence and a remotely valid canonical tag. Schema 3.3.0 prevents recurrence for new checkpoints; remote publication validation still remains mandatory after the tag is pushed.

title: An editing path that consumes a backslash escape leaves a control character, and the control it belonged to silently matches nothing
symptom: A frontend control scan compiled, ran and reported success while matching zero elements. Its regular expression contained a literal backspace where a word-boundary escape belonged, so it could never match anything.
rootCauseSummary: The test was edited through a path that consumed the backslash escape, and the resulting control character survived into the file. Nothing downstream could tell an empty corpus from a clean one, so the control reported the delivery as clean.
resolution: Two controls. A repository-wide scan refuses a stray control character in any source file, which prevents the class rather than the instance; and every scan in this Gate asserts that it found something to judge before judging it.

prevention.description: No source file under tests, scripts, packages, services or the API carries a control character other than tab, newline or carriage return.
The null control: the same scan fires on a mangled fixture and stays quiet on an intact one.
The scan asserts that it found controls to inspect before judging them.
The boundary scan asserts a non-empty corpus.

applicability.requiredCheck: Confirm that every scan this Gate adds asserts it found something before judging it, and that no source file carries a stray control character.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A green run of the repository-wide control-character scan and of each scan's own non-empty-corpus assertion.

provenance.notes: Derived from this Gate's own recorded failure; no content outside this repository was used.

notes: The residual limit is that a scan can still be wrong in ways an empty-corpus assertion does not see: it can read the wrong corpus, or match a pattern that is merely too narrow. What the control removes is the failure mode where the corpus is empty and nothing says so.

title: A naming convention rewrites a CHECK constraint's name and leaves a UNIQUE constraint's alone
symptom: Dropping a check constraint by its full name produced ALTER TABLE task_runs DROP CONSTRAINT ck_task_runs_ck_task_runs_status_is_known, and creating a unique constraint by its full name produced one the downgrade could not find, which failed three migration suites at once.
rootCauseSummary: The declarative naming convention is applied only when the template for that constraint kind contains the constraint-name token. The CHECK template does; the UNIQUE template does not. So a check constraint is named by its bare name and a unique constraint keeps exactly what it is given, and using one rule for both is wrong in one direction or the other.
resolution: The migration creates and drops a check constraint by its bare name and a unique constraint by exactly the name the model declares, and states the asymmetry in a comment where the code is. The reversibility test applies and reverses the migration against a disposable database, so a mismatch is a failing test rather than a failed downgrade in an incident.

prevention.description: The migration is applied and reversed against a disposable database, which is what a name mismatch breaks.
Autogenerate against a freshly migrated database finds nothing left to do, which a name mismatch would report.
The migration uses the bare name for a check constraint.
The migration uses the declared name for a unique constraint, on both sides.
Current strengthened causal boundary; every original control remains.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every migration this Gate adds, confirm it is applied and reversed against a disposable database, and that autogenerate finds nothing left to do afterwards.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A green reversibility run and a green autogenerate check against a database migrated from zero.

guardrailFailures.detail: GUARDRAIL_FAILURE: G6-INT-003: The new ORM UNIQUE names assumed the convention prefixes explicit names as CHECK does. LSN-0042 already distinguishes these naming rules; escalate the guarded recurrence and align actual explicit UNIQUE names, preserving the unchanged real migration assertion.

provenance.notes: Derived from this Gate's own recorded failure; no content outside this repository was used.

Causal acceptance: actual complete pre-live cmd-0054; actual PostgreSQL/HTTP/migrations36 cmd-0050 and exact fresh real provider/sandbox/quality experience producer. The prior integration attempt's false identity flag is retained without inventing its cause. Guards restored, not whole-Gate readiness: immutable full verification and ordered assurance remain pending.

title: A log line is not evidence that another process is ready
symptom: A scenario waited for a worker's start-up line, started a run, and then waited out its whole two-minute timeout on a run that had never been scheduled.
rootCauseSummary: The worker prints that it started before it begins polling, so the line reports an intention rather than a state. The observable fact is the one the server holds: whether the task queue has a poller.
resolution: The scenario asks Temporal's DescribeTaskQueue through the harness, which is the same question the worker's own container healthcheck asks, and waits on the answer rather than on the narration.

prevention.description: The scenario's readiness wait asks the server for the poller count.
The readiness wait does not read container logs.
The harness implements the question against the workflow service rather than against a file.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every wait this Gate adds on another process, confirm it asks that process or its server for the state rather than reading a log line.
applicability.requiredEvidence: The readiness path asserted against the server's own answer, with the log-line path refused by a test.

provenance.notes: Derived from this Gate's own recorded failure; no content outside this repository was used.

notes: The residual limit is that the server's answer is also a snapshot: a poller can disappear between the answer and the next call. What the control removes is the case where the wait was never about the queue at all.

title: A boundary scan must read the code rather than the prose, and must be shown to fire on a mutated module
symptom: Three boundary scans reported escapes on their first run, every one a false positive: a docstring that explained why the runtime names no provider, a deny-list that refuses an authorisation header, and a call to str.replace read as os.replace.
rootCauseSummary: Each scan matched text. A scan that reads prose forces the explanation out of the file, a scan that reads a deny-list cannot tell a defence from the thing it defends against, and a scan that matches the last segment of a call cannot tell two unrelated functions apart.
resolution: Every boundary scan reads the abstract syntax tree: imports by module, calls by their full dotted name, and identifiers with docstrings excluded. Each one carries a null control that runs the identical scan over a module which does the forbidden thing and requires it to fire.

prevention.description: The execution scans fire on a module that imports subprocess, writes a file or calls eval, and stay quiet on ordinary code.
The provider scan fires on a module that names a provider in code and not on one that discusses it in a docstring.
Each of the four ways a credential could enter is detected on a mutated module.
The repository-wide execution scan fires on a mutated module and stays quiet on a clean one.
The workflow determinism scan fires on a module that reads a clock and a random value.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every boundary scan this Gate adds, confirm it reads the syntax tree rather than the text, and that it carries a control which runs the identical scan over a module that violates the rule.
applicability.requiredEvidence: Each scan's null control executed and green, alongside the scan itself.

provenance.notes: Derived from this Gate's own recorded failure; no content outside this repository was used.

notes: The residual limit is that an abstract syntax tree describes one language. A scan over a template, a configuration file or a shell script is still a text scan, and its null control matters more there, not less.

title: A counted test suite must declare its cases statically, because the denominator is read from the source
symptom: Ninety-five cases of the ledger suite errored at once, all of them on the same message: a test in a counted suite is parametrised and the TESTS denominator cannot reproduce a runtime expansion.
rootCauseSummary: The denominator is derived by reading the source, so a case produced at run time by a parametrisation cannot be counted. The counter already refuses one, but it refuses from inside the counting step, several layers below the file that caused it, so the failure arrives as a wall of unrelated-looking errors rather than as a statement about one function.
resolution: Every case in a counted pytest suite is written as a loop over a module-level tuple, which counts as one case and covers the same inputs. A repository test asks the same question of the same files and fails fast, naming the file and the function.

prevention.description: No test function in a counted pytest suite carries a parametrisation.
The null control: the same scan fires on a parametrised module and stays quiet on a plain one.

applicability.requiredCheck: Confirm that every case this Gate adds to a counted suite is declared statically, with table-driven inputs written as a loop rather than as a parametrisation.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A green run of the counted-suite scan alongside the suite itself.

guardrailFailures.detail: GUARDRAIL_FAILURE: cmd-0105: Gate 4 added parametrised cases to counted evaluator and sandbox suites despite GRD-0047; the mandatory tests gate failed while deriving its static denominator.

provenance.notes: Derived from this Gate's recorded full-verification failure; no content outside this repository was used.

notes: Recurrence 1, GATE-4-CP-0001 cmd-0105: GRD-0047 did detect the recurrence when the mandatory suite finally ran, but the Gate 4 implementation had already added the prohibited decorators. All affected cases are now explicit loops. The residual limit remains that the scan recognizes parametrisation decorators, not every possible dynamic generator.

title: A timeout that cancels the task it runs in leaves nothing able to record what happened
symptom: A run with a ten-second deadline was still RUNNING two minutes later. Temporal showed the workflow had in fact ended at 10.07 seconds, failed with 'Activity cancelled', having written nothing: no state change, no event, no reason. The row stayed RUNNING for ever.
rootCauseSummary: Two faults in the same three lines. The deadline was `asyncio.wait_for`, which from Python 3.11 implements its timeout by cancelling the task that awaits it — here the workflow's own — so the next activity it scheduled was cancelled before it started. And the wait on the cancelled work expected `CancelledError`, while Temporal surfaces a cancelled activity as `ActivityError`, so the handler never ran. A deadline enforced against the process rather than against the run looks identical to no deadline at all from the outside, because the only difference is a record nobody wrote.
resolution: The engine runs as an explicit child task raced against a timer, so cancellation stays in the child and the workflow's own task is never left cancelling. The wait on that child accepts every way a cancelled activity surfaces. The deadline path then writes the state, the event and the reason from a task that is still able to write.

prevention.description: A real run against a real workflow must reach FAILED with RUN_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED and a RUN_FAILED event; this is the control that found the defect.
The deadline may not be a timeout that cancels the workflow's own task.
The handler expects ActivityError as well as CancelledError.
The deadline path sets the state, records the event and names the reason.
The scenario asserts the record, not only the ending.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every limit this Gate enforces, confirm that the enforcement path is still able to write when it fires, and that a real run is observed reaching the terminal state with the reason recorded.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A recorded scenario run in which the limit fires and the store shows the terminal state, the error type and the event.

provenance.notes: Derived from this Gate's own recorded failure and from the Temporal history of the run that exposed it; no content outside this repository was used.

notes: The residual limit is that the static half of this control describes one shape of the mistake. A future deadline written some third way would pass the scans; what actually protects the claim is the scenario, which asks the store what the run became and would fail again.

title: A refusal that misnames the defect spends the only repair on the wrong correction
symptom: The first live planner-reviewer run failed INVALID_AGENT_OUTPUT: the planner answered twice and was refused twice with 'a FINAL envelope must carry non-empty content'. One diagnostic call through the gateway showed the answer did carry content - a JSON array of two plan steps.
rootCauseSummary: The parser tested 'is a non-empty string' and reported every failure of that test as missing content, so a present value of the wrong type was described as an absent one. The runtime's one repair quotes the refusal back to the model, which then corrected a defect it did not have and returned the same array. Underneath, the runtime contract never said that content is a string, and a planner asked for one step per line reads that as a list.
resolution: A present content of the wrong type is refused with its own reason, content-not-a-string, in a sentence that names the JSON type found and says that a multi-line answer is still one string. The runtime instructions state, once and for every agent, that content is one JSON string and never an array or an object. The parser accepts nothing it refused before.

prevention.description: An array, an object, a number and a boolean are each refused as content-not-a-string, the sentence names the type and never says missing, and absent or blank content keeps missing-content.
The contract every agent receives names the type of content.
The live planner-reviewer run, the control that found the defect: team.succeeded fails when a stage is refused twice.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every validator whose refusal is sent back as the instruction to correct - to a model through a repair, or to a user - confirm that each distinct defect (absent, wrong type, wrong value) has its own reason, and that a wrong-typed value is never reported as missing.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A test per defect class asserting the reason code and that the sentence names the defect it found.

provenance.notes: Derived from this Gate's own live smoke runs and one diagnostic call that printed only the shape of the model's answer; no content outside this repository was used.

notes: The residual limit is coverage of shapes: the tests enumerate the JSON types a model can put in content, and a validator elsewhere in the repository that fuses two defects into one sentence would not be caught by them. The requiredCheck is what carries the rule to the next validator.

title: A state and the event that explains it, written in two commits, are written event first
symptom: A live single-agent run read SUCCEEDED while its event log held six events and no RUN_COMPLETED. The run before it and the run after it had all seven: the defect showed once in three runs, only to a reader that waited for a terminal state and then read the log.
rootCauseSummary: The engine committed the terminal state and then, in a second activity, the terminal event. Anything reading between the two saw a finished run whose log had not finished - the live smoke, and an SSE stream opened on a finished run, which ends at once because the state is terminal and so never delivers the terminal event. The workflow's deadline and unrecoverable paths used the same order, and the API's workflow-could-not-start path wrote FAILED with no terminal event at all.
resolution: Every terminal path writes the terminal event first and the terminal state second: the engine's SUCCEEDED, FAILED and CANCELLED, the workflow's deadline and unrecoverable paths, and the API path that fails a run whose workflow never started, which now records RUN_FAILED. A reader that sees a terminal state therefore always finds the log closed; the reverse window, a closed log over a row one activity behind, is the half a reader can act on safely.

prevention.description: For a succeeded, a failed and a cancelled run, the log already holds the terminal event at the moment the terminal state is written.
In the workflow's deadline and unrecoverable paths every record_event precedes every set_state.
The API records RUN_FAILED before it writes FAILED when the workflow cannot start.
The live check that found it: single.events_persisted requires RUN_COMPLETED once the run reads SUCCEEDED.

applicability.requiredCheck: Wherever a state and the record that explains it are written in separate commits, confirm which one a reader between the two can see alone, and that it is the one a reader may act on - the record before the state it explains.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A test that observes what the log held at the moment each terminal state was written.

provenance.notes: Derived from this Gate's own live smoke runs and one diagnostic call that printed only the shape of the model's answer; no content outside this repository was used.

notes: The residual limit is that the order is two commits and not one. A reader can still see a closed log over a row that is one activity behind, and a crash between the two leaves that until Temporal retries the second activity. Writing both in one transaction removes the window entirely and needs a new store operation; it is recorded as a risk rather than done inside a closure.

title: A metric read the instant after the call that moved it is read before the scrape that carries it
symptom: The live gateway smoke failed one check of twenty on a call that had succeeded: observability.scraped found no gateway request series. The stack had been rebuilt seconds before, so the API's counter had restarted and Prometheus had not scraped it since the smoke's own requests.
rootCauseSummary: The check asked Prometheus once, immediately after the inference, while Prometheus scrapes the API every fifteen seconds. Whether the counter had been scraped yet was a matter of timing, so the check passed on a stack that had been running for a while and failed on a freshly started one - the result described the clock, not the gateway.
resolution: Every Prometheus target observation now uses one policy-derived helper bounded by three versioned scrape intervals and polling only Prometheus; neither the action nor the stack is retried.

prevention.description: A scrape that arrives after the call is waited for, one that never arrives fails within the bound, and every read goes to Prometheus.
The live check still makes exactly one inference and one stream.
Every script that reads Prometheus's API waits for a scrape within a bound; the control is the class, read from the syntax tree.
The null control of that scan.
The Foundation smoke waits for both targets and asks only Prometheus.
The infrastructure and smoke paths share the versioned scrape-cycle budget and do not repeat the observed action.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every check that reads what another process observes on its own cycle - a scrape, a poll, a flush - confirm that the check waits for at least one full cycle, with a bound, and never repeats the action it is observing to make the observation appear.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A test in which the observation arrives only after a delay, and the check still passes within its bound.

guardrailFailures.detail: GUARDRAIL_FAILURE: G2-F-014: the Foundation smoke read Prometheus target health before the scrape that followed a fresh installation and reported both IACode targets down. GRD-0051 named one function in the gateway smoke, not the class.

GUARDRAIL_FAILURE: G4-F-002 exposed that the running-stack infrastructure test sampled Prometheus target health immediately after a clean stack start. GRD-0051 scanned scripts but did not cover the infrastructure test path that queried the same asynchronous observer.

provenance.notes: Derived from repository-recorded live verification failures; no content outside this repository was used.

notes: The residual limit is that the check proves the required target is healthy within the declared scrape budget, not that an arbitrary historical sample is current. Recurrence 2 widened the control from scripts to the infrastructure test path and centralized the observer policy.

title: A checkpoint sealed without naming its own tag cannot be validated from that tag
symptom: Once GATE-2-CP-0002 anchored its predecessor, test_every_sealed_checkpoint_validates_from_its_own_tag failed for GATE-2-CP-0001: 'detached HEAD validation requires STATE.json currentCommit to name the checkpoint tag'. The checkpoint had been sealed at BLOCKED with currentCommit HEAD and had never been valid from its own tag.
rootCauseSummary: Three rules disagreed. The protocol lets a work-in-progress status keep the symbolic HEAD; the seal tool sealed whatever state it was given; and validation from a tag required the state to spell that tag. A checkpoint sealed at BLOCKED satisfied the first two and could never satisfy the third, and nothing looked until a successor anchored it.
resolution: With a detached HEAD, a symbolic HEAD is bound to the checkpoint's own canonical tag derived from its identity - the same binding a named tag gives, and still refused anywhere else. The seal tool refuses a state that does not name its own tag, so no further checkpoint is sealed that way. ADR-0023.

prevention.description: The seal is refused, and no tag is created, when currentCommit is not the checkpoint's own canonical tag.
A checkpoint that kept the symbolic HEAD validates from its own tag.
The same state checked out anywhere but at its tag is refused.
Every anchored checkpoint is validated from its own tag.

applicability.requiredCheck: Before sealing a checkpoint at any status, confirm that STATE.json currentCommit names the checkpoint's own canonical tag, and that the sealed content validates from that tag with a detached HEAD.
applicability.requiredEvidence: The post-seal validation from the checkpoint's own tag, and the seal tool's refusal of a state that does not name it.

guardrailFailures.detail: GUARDRAIL_FAILURE: cmd-0144 refused checkpoint validation after the pre-commit finalizer had moved an unsealed working tree to READY_FOR_REVIEW and named a canonical tag that could not yet resolve. The run was returned to IN_PROGRESS before any seal or publication and the full assurance order is being repeated.

provenance.notes: Derived from this checkpoint's own recorded suite failure; no content outside this repository was used.

notes: The residual limit is that the derived binding trusts the checkpoint directory's name as its identity; the anchor chain, which records each checkpoint's tag and commit, is what detects a directory and a tag that were moved together. Recurrence 1, GATE-4-CP-0003 cmd-0144: finalization was invoked before the last Green Keeper cycle, so the terminal-state validator correctly refused the unresolved pre-seal tag; the checkpoint was reverted to IN_PROGRESS and assurance is repeated before finalization.

title: A payload one service bounds for another must be bounded as the receiver measures it
symptom: The sandbox bounded a tool's raw output to 128 KiB, and the agent runtime refuses a tool result above 256 KiB measured as canonical JSON. A file of control characters inside the read limit renders at 768 KiB, so the runtime would have failed the run that read it.
rootCauseSummary: Two limits on one payload lived in two services and measured two different things: raw bytes on the producer, the escaped JSON rendering on the consumer. Neither service's suite could see the other's measure.
resolution: The sandbox shortens what it hands an agent to SANDBOX_AGENT_RESULT_MAX_BYTES, measured exactly as the runtime measures, explicitly and keeping every artifact reference; a repository test reads both limits from their sources and requires the consumer's to be the larger.

prevention.description: Both limits are read from their sources; the receiver's is at least the sender's.
An output that renders three times over the bound is shortened to it, explicitly.
The null control: an ordinary output passes the same path unchanged.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every payload one service bounds and another service accepts or refuses by size, confirm both measure it the same way and that the receiver's bound is not smaller than what the sender may hand over.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A test that reads both bounds from their sources and compares them, and a test that the sender's bound holds for the worst-case rendering.

provenance.notes: Derived from this checkpoint's own recorded runs and repairs; no content outside this repository was used.

notes: The residual limit is the runtime's context: several large results in one stage can still exceed the assembled context bound, which the runtime refuses explicitly rather than truncating.

title: Two processes that meet on a queue must name what crosses it once, and a real run must exercise both
symptom: The first real coding run never finished: its workflow task failed with KeyError 'agentResult'. The sandbox's activity answered with the execution record alone, and the workflow read the tool result under a key the answer did not carry.
rootCauseSummary: The producer and the consumer of one activity result spelled its shape separately, in two processes, and each side's suite drove the other side as a double, so both suites were green over an incompatible pair.
resolution: The keys are named once in iacode_contracts.sandbox and used on both sides; the sandbox suite runs the activity as Temporal runs it; a repository scan refuses a literal spelling of either key on either side; and the coding scenario exercises the real pair.

prevention.description: The workflow and the activity both use the shared names, and neither spells them.
The null control: a workflow that spells the key itself is detected.
The activity, run by Temporal's test environment, answers under the shared keys.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every payload this Gate sends between two processes, confirm its names are defined once in a shared contract, used by both sides, and exercised once by a run in which neither side is a double.
applicability.requiredEvidence: The shared definition, a scan of both sides for a literal spelling, and a recorded run through the real producer and consumer.

provenance.notes: Derived from this checkpoint's own recorded runs and repairs; no content outside this repository was used.

notes: The scan covers the keys of this one activity. A new activity result is covered only when its keys are added to the shared contract and to the scan.

title: A process sweep that reads what a forking process holds waits on the processes it has to kill
symptom: A fork bomb that detached from its command wedged a sandbox: the sweep after the command killed a handful of processes in fifteen seconds, the survivors refilled the process table, and the next command could not be started.
rootCauseSummary: The sweep read every process's command line, which takes that process's memory lock, held by a process in the middle of a fork; and it killed without stopping first, so every slot it freed was refilled before its next round.
resolution: The sweep lists processes and reads only their state, stops every one until no new process appears, kills them, and remains inside its bounded loop until /proc proves the init has reaped the resulting zombies.

prevention.description: A detached bomb is swept and the sandbox answers the next command with an empty process table.
A bomb that stays attached is contained by the limit and ended at its timeout.
The same sweep ends a command's escaped children.
The deterministic sweep does not return while a zombie still occupies the PID cgroup.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every control that must end processes it did not start, confirm it freezes before it kills, reads nothing a forking process holds, waits for killed processes to leave the PID table, and is attacked on the real engine by a process that detaches and forks.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A deterministic zombie-reaping control plus an engine test in which a detached fork bomb is swept and the next command still runs.

guardrailFailures.detail: GUARDRAIL_FAILURE: cmd-0062 reproduced the detached fork-bomb liveness failure: every live process was killed, but the sweep returned while zombies could still occupy the PID limit and the next command could not start.

provenance.notes: Derived from this checkpoint's own recorded runs and repairs; no content outside this repository was used.

notes: The sweep remains bounded to fifteen seconds; the recurrence showed that an all-zombie process table is not empty because zombies still consume the PID limit until init reaps them.

title: A pre-push check narrower than the change's reach lets a red gate reach the public remote
symptom: Three pushed commits left a mandatory gate red: the first broke the repository-wide decoding scan, two later ones the lint gate. Each ran the suites of what it changed, not the repository-wide gates the change could reach.
rootCauseSummary: The pre-push check was chosen by the commit's subject rather than by its reach: a new script is reached by the scans over every script, and any source file by the lint gate.
resolution: Each was repaired by a new commit, never an amend; from then on every push ran the lint gate and the repository-wide scans in addition to the suites of the change.

prevention.description: Before each push: status, the staged diff, a secret scan of the staged content and the tests the change can reach.

applicability.requiredCheck: Before each push, run the lint gate and the repository-wide scans as well as the suites of the change, because a change reaches every control that scans the tree.
applicability.requiredEvidence: Recorded lint and targeted runs between each push and the one before it.

provenance.notes: Derived from this checkpoint's own recorded runs and repairs; no content outside this repository was used.

notes: Not guarded: the ledger's first pushes of this Gate predate the practice, so a control over the ledger would refuse the history that taught it; the Green Keeper's full cycle at closure is what catches a gate left red. Recurred in GATE-3-CP-0003: GATE-3-CP-0003: commit 3101d31 (M1-F-001) was pushed after its targeted tests and staged scan but before the lint gate, which was red on a 101-character comment line in protocol.py (cmd-0052); the next commit restored it (cmd-0053, 369f084).

title: A contract a model must follow has to reach the model, rendered from the definition the parser enforces
symptom: With the operator's configured model the developer stage never produced a valid tool request: the arguments were written at the top level of the envelope, then under 'args' after the one repair, and the run failed INVALID_AGENT_OUTPUT. A second model made two valid requests, then failed the same way.
rootCauseSummary: The runtime described a tool request only as a tool that 'carries its name and arguments' and never showed the keys. The schema that named them reached a model only as a structured-output request, made only for a model whose capability is known, and the configured provider declares none; the docstring said the schema documented the prompt, and nothing checked that it did. The parser also dropped a stray key in the tool object, so an argument sent under 'args' was lost silently and refused later by the sandbox.
resolution: protocol.envelope_contract renders the version, every kind, one minimal valid envelope per kind with tool.name and tool.arguments, and where the arguments go, from envelope_schema() and the kind table the parser enforces. The runtime instructions carry it on every turn and the repair restates it verbatim with the stage's tools; the parser refuses a key beside name and arguments by its own reason. A live coding run of the configured model then made eleven valid tool requests, all executed in the sandbox, with no repair.

prevention.description: The instructions carry the contract rendered from the schema, verbatim, with the stage's tools.
The repair restates the same contract.
A change of the canonical schema changes the rendered text.
The instructions module spells no envelope key of its own.
Arguments outside tool.arguments are refused by their real defect.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every structured answer a model must produce, confirm that the exact shape is in the text every model receives — rendered from the definition the parser enforces, not written beside it — and that a live run of the configured model produces it.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A test that the instructions contain the rendered shape and follow a change of the schema, and a live run of the configured model that produces the shape.

provenance.notes: Derived from the M1 fresh-session audit's findings and this corrective delivery's recorded executions; no content outside this repository was used.

notes: The residual limit is the model: the shape is shown and a malformed answer is refused, but whether a given model follows the contract, and whether it finishes a task within its budget, is measured by live runs, not guaranteed. The configured model's run made valid requests and exhausted its turns without finishing the task.

title: A result is accepted only from the executor that owns the request, decided when the request is created
symptom: In the deterministic timeout scenario, a SUCCEEDED result posted to the API while the sandbox executed the command was answered 200; the stored result was the forged one, the sandbox's own execution record still said TIMED_OUT, and the agent answered TIMEOUT-NOT-SEEN.
rootCauseSummary: resolve_tool_request accepted any PENDING request of the run whatever its executor, and the workflow resumed the agent with the stored result, answering the sandbox's later delivery with the first one. Nothing recorded that a sandboxed stage's request is answered by the sandbox, so every door looked the same.
resolution: A tool request records its executor when it is created: SANDBOX for a stage with a sandbox policy, EXTERNAL otherwise (migration 0005). The store takes the origin of a result from the caller's code path — the API's service passes EXTERNAL, the workflow's internal activity passes SANDBOX — and refuses a mismatch with TOOL_RESULT_ORIGIN_REFUSED (403) before anything is stored or signalled. The audit's null control and mutation are a verification stage.

prevention.description: A forged result before and after the sandbox's own is refused and the stored result is the sandbox's.
A manual result for a sandbox request is refused and nothing is stored.
The API answers 403 TOOL_RESULT_ORIGIN_REFUSED and signals nothing.
Every caller passes a constant origin, never one read from a payload; the scan fires on a mutated source.
Existing requests keep their meaning through the migration.
The verification stage sandbox-tool-result-origin: the audit's null control and mutation on the real stack.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every result, verdict or callback that more than one producer could deliver, confirm that the owner is recorded when the work is created, that the origin of a delivery comes from the code path and never from the delivery, and that a delivery from any other origin is refused before it is stored.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A test that a delivery from the wrong origin is refused before and after the owner's, with a null control through the same path, and a run on the real stack.

provenance.notes: Derived from the M1 fresh-session audit's findings and this corrective delivery's recorded executions; no content outside this repository was used.

notes: The residual limit is the M1 trust model: the API is unauthenticated on the loopback interface and Temporal is internal, so a local process that can schedule the worker's activities directly could still act as the sandbox. The control closes the public door, which is the one the audit found open.

title: A pinned lock can become unsafe without changing, so advisory state is live evidence
symptom: A sealed delivery whose implementation checks passed later failed the unchanged dependency gate with two Critical and four High npm advisories in its pinned graph.
rootCauseSummary: The lockfile was reproducible but advisory state changed after it was pinned. Reproducibility fixes the graph; it does not make the graph permanently safe.
resolution: Update the direct frontend pins and resolved lock graph to non-vulnerable versions, then require a live scan of both npm and PyPI advisory sources before handoff.

prevention.description: The mandatory scan fails closed when either advisory source is unavailable and blocks every relevant Critical or High finding.
The dependency scanner's blocking severities and fail-closed source policy are structural assertions, so weakening either turns the suite red.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every pinned dependency graph delivered by a Gate, run the current advisory scan against every required source and refuse Critical or High findings without suppressing advisories or narrowing the denominator.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A report from every required advisory source showing zero relevant Critical or High findings, plus a test that proves those severities remain blocking.

provenance.notes: Derived from the sealed M1 fresh-session audit; no content outside this repository was used.

notes: The residual limit is time: a green scan is evidence about the advisory databases at execution time, so every later release still needs a fresh scan.

title: Container health does not prove Docker Desktop host-port forwarding
symptom: The complete verifier and two targeted reruns found Grafana, MinIO and Redis accepting host connections and immediately closing them, while Compose reported every affected container healthy.
rootCauseSummary: Docker Desktop's host-side published-port forwarding had entered a stale state. Container-local health checks remained green, so health alone could not observe it.
resolution: Restart the full stack without deleting volumes, wait for every service to recover, and repeat the live host-facing infrastructure suite. The unchanged 49-test suite then passed.

prevention.description: Live tests connect through the actual loopback-published Grafana, MinIO and Redis ports instead of trusting container health metadata.

applicability.requiredCheck: Exercise every required host-published service through its actual loopback port; do not substitute container health for host reachability.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A live host-facing infrastructure suite after stack health, with the original failure retained if a non-destructive restart is required for recovery.

provenance.notes: Derived only from this checkpoint's recorded verifier and recovery runs.

notes: The guardrail detects the host-path failure; recovery remains an environment action and never converts the original failed run into a pass.

title: A lesson exclusion must declare the scope it excludes
symptom: The full suite rejected LSN-0058 because technology and module selectors excluded it from a generic preflight while its scopes list was empty.
rootCauseSummary: Applicability dimensions were used as incidental metadata. In this model they are selectors, so they silently narrowed where the lesson constrained delivery.
resolution: Remove selectors that were not intended to narrow LSN-0058. Reserve non-empty selectors for deliberate exclusions, with scopes naming the boundary explicitly.

prevention.description: Every active lesson excluded from a canonical preflight must carry a non-empty scopes declaration that makes the exclusion reviewable.

applicability.requiredCheck: Confirm every active lesson excluded from a preflight declares a non-empty scope selector, and that incidental metadata does not narrow applicability.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A passing repository-preflight coverage test over the complete active lesson set.

guardrailFailures.detail: GUARDRAIL_FAILURE: Green Keeper cmd-0121 refused LSN-0102 because an incidental development-ledger module selector excluded it from the canonical generic preflight while its scopes list was empty.

provenance.notes: Derived from cmd-0064 and its targeted repair proof in cmd-0069; the cmd-0121 recurrence is preserved in CP0009's command ledger.

notes: The control checks explicit exclusions; it cannot decide whether a deliberately declared scope is semantically the best boundary. Cmd-0121 demonstrated the guardrail remained effective by refusing the repeated incidental-selector failure.

title: Parent and child facts without an ORM relationship require an explicit flush boundary
symptom: The first real PostgreSQL quality-plan insert attempted to persist quality_checks before their quality_plans parent and failed its foreign key, although both objects had been added to one SQLAlchemy session.
rootCauseSummary: The store assigned the foreign-key UUID directly but declared no ORM relationship between the newly created plan and check objects. The unit of work therefore had no object dependency edge that guaranteed the parent insert first.
resolution: Insert and flush the quality plan before adding its checks, and insert and flush a quality run before adding its initial event. Keep the real PostgreSQL lifecycle test in complete verification.

prevention.description: The real PostgreSQL integration creates the plan with its child checks, creates the run with its first event, and reads the complete lifecycle back.

applicability.requiredCheck: Whenever one transaction inserts parent and child ORM facts using raw foreign-key identifiers without a relationship edge, confirm the parent is flushed before the child is added.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A real-database integration test that creates the parent and child together and observes both after commit.

provenance.notes: Derived from the first Gate 4 PostgreSQL persistence execution; no external content was used.

notes: The explicit flush is needed because the objects are connected only by UUID values; adding an ORM relationship would also create the dependency edge but is unnecessary for this write path.

title: Cancellation completion must not bypass cleanup acknowledgement
symptom: The rebuilt evaluator suite failed because its late-callback test tried to transition a running quality run directly to CANCELLED.
rootCauseSummary: The test used the terminal label as setup and skipped the CANCELLING state that records the cancellation request and reserves time for sandbox cleanup acknowledgement.
resolution: Drive the test through RUNNING to CANCELLING with CANCELLATION_REQUESTED, then to CANCELLED with COMPLETED before testing rejection of a late callback.

prevention.description: The store test executes both cancellation transitions and then proves that a callback delivered after cleanup completion is refused.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every running task that can be cancelled, prove the lifecycle records cancellation requested before it records cancellation completed.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A lifecycle test that enters the intermediate cancelling state, acknowledges cleanup, reaches cancelled, and rejects late delivery.

provenance.notes: Derived from the recorded evaluator failure cmd-0029; no external content was used.

notes: Runs that have not started may still cancel directly where no executor cleanup acknowledgement is required.

title: Provenance digests are a set even when their sources are distinct
symptom: The first workflow-adapter test failed when the snapshot and policy fixtures intentionally shared a digest, because the evidence contract refuses duplicate sourceDigests.
rootCauseSummary: The activity treated semantic source slots as if they implied distinct content hashes. Two different source roles may legitimately resolve to identical bytes, while the evidence contract records the unique content set.
resolution: Deduplicate source digests by value while preserving their first-seen order before constructing immutable evidence.

prevention.description: The adapter test uses equal snapshot and policy digests and proves that redacted evidence is still accepted and persisted once.

applicability.requiredCheck: Whenever provenance is represented by content digests, normalize it as a unique ordered set rather than assuming each semantic source has different bytes.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A test in which distinct provenance roles share one digest and the stored provenance contains it once.

provenance.notes: Derived from the Gate 4 focused adapter execution; no external content was used.

notes: Digest deduplication does not erase semantic provenance because the evidence contract records content identities, not a labelled source-role map.

title: An identity shared across services must satisfy the strictest persistence type and remain stable
symptom: The first end-to-end quality run reached the sandbox and failed when its readable quality-check identity was parsed for a UUID database column.
rootCauseSummary: The evaluator treated toolRequestId as an opaque string while the shared sandbox store persists it as UUID. The contract's syntax was looser than the receiver's durable representation.
resolution: Derive each quality execution identity as UUIDv5 from the immutable run and check identities, retaining both retry stability and database compatibility.

prevention.description: The same run and check always derive the same valid UUID, while another check derives a different one.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every identity crossing a service boundary, verify it satisfies the strictest persisted representation and is stable across delivery retries.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A contract or unit test proving syntactic validity, deterministic replay identity and separation between distinct work items.

provenance.notes: Derived from the first Gate 4 execution through the real evaluator and sandbox; no external content was used.

notes: UUIDv5 exposes no secret and encodes identity, not content; the namespace and input prefix keep this use separate from unrelated UUID derivations.

title: A shared execution resource needs an explicit exclusive owner for every owning domain

source.finding: first live sandbox persistence for a quality run

symptom: A real evaluator run could not create its sandbox session because sandbox_sessions required task_run_id even though no task run owned the quality run.
rootCauseSummary: Gate 3 encoded the then-only owner in the table shape. Reusing the sandbox from a second durable domain without evolving ownership would have required a fake task run or a nullable unowned session.
resolution: Add quality_run_id, constrain exactly one owner with num_nonnulls, and enforce a separate one-active-session partial unique index for each owner domain.

prevention.description: The declared model requires one and only one owner and one active slot for both task and quality runs.
Real PostgreSQL accepts a quality-owned session through the lifecycle.

applicability.requiredCheck: When another durable domain reuses an owned resource, model its real ownership explicitly, require exactly one owner, and preserve every per-owner exclusivity invariant.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A structural test of the ownership and uniqueness constraints plus a real-database lifecycle test for the new owner.

provenance.notes: Derived from Gate 4's real PostgreSQL sandbox session creation; no external content was used.

notes: The model is intentionally exclusive rather than polymorphic text: both possible owners retain real foreign keys and cascade behavior.

title: A shared execution identifier must not be written into a foreign key owned by another domain

source.finding: live evaluator sandbox execution after owner migration

symptom: After the session gained a quality owner, execution still failed when active_tool_request_id tried to reference the evaluator's stable UUID in tool_requests, where only agent-runtime requests exist.
rootCauseSummary: The sandbox used one request shape for two domains but treated every request identifier as an agent tool-request foreign key. Syntactic compatibility did not imply ownership compatibility.
resolution: Bind active_tool_request_id only when agentRunId proves an agent-runtime owner; evaluator execution remains durable through its quality result and session owner.

prevention.description: An evaluator request yields no agent FK while an agent request preserves its durable tool-request reference.

applicability.requiredCheck: For a shared execution contract, prove each durable foreign key is populated only for the domain that owns the referenced row, using trusted ownership context rather than identifier shape.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A test with both owner domains showing that only the owning domain binds the foreign key.

provenance.notes: Derived from Gate 4's real evaluator-to-sandbox persistence failure; no external content was used.

notes: The quality request UUID remains useful for idempotent execution records; it simply is not an agent tool_requests primary key.

title: Immutable content identity excludes observation time and the first observer
symptom: Re-running the same snapshot and policy conflicted with its existing frozen quality plan because createdAt and the first owner differed.
rootCauseSummary: The reuse check compared the complete serialized record rather than the material inputs that define plan content, so observational metadata was mistaken for a conflicting plan definition.
resolution: Compare plan material identity from snapshot, policy, project profile and frozen checks while retaining the original immutable creation time and owner as provenance.

prevention.description: The same material plan reuses one row despite a later observation time and a different owner.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every content-addressed or reusable immutable record, define material identity separately from creation metadata and ownership provenance.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A replay test where material inputs are equal but time and first observer differ, proving reuse without rewriting the original record.

provenance.notes: Derived from the Gate 4 reproduction scenario; no external content was used.

notes: Observation metadata remains immutable evidence on the first record; it is excluded only from equality of the plan's material definition.

title: Cancellation semantics must survive orchestration-library exception wrapping
symptom: The sandbox acknowledged cancellation and cleaned up, but the evaluator persisted ERROR because Temporal delivered the cancelled activity as ActivityError rather than asyncio.CancelledError.
rootCauseSummary: The workflow classified the Python exception wrapper instead of combining the durable cancellation request with the sandbox's acknowledged activity cancellation semantics.
resolution: When cancellation was requested, translate the activity failure that completes WAIT_CANCELLATION_COMPLETED into a CANCELLED quality result and preserve ERROR for activity failures without that request.

prevention.description: A cancellation-requested activity wrapped as ActivityError produces CANCELLED, while the non-cancelled error path remains distinct.

applicability.requiredCheck: For cancellation across an orchestration boundary, test the exception shape the real library delivers and derive outcome from the durable request plus executor acknowledgement rather than the wrapper class alone.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A workflow test for the wrapped cancellation and a live running-cancellation scenario proving cleanup, terminal cancellation and idempotent repeat.

provenance.notes: Derived from the Gate 4 Temporal workflow and real sandbox cancellation scenario; no external content was used.

notes: The mapping is conditioned on a durable cancellation request; an unrelated ActivityError is still an execution error and cannot masquerade as cancellation.

title: A bounded parser must apply each content limit only to content it interprets
symptom: The complete functional battery passed six scenario classes but could not evaluate the IACode snapshot because a large canonical-requirements JSON file was rejected as an oversized project manifest.
rootCauseSummary: detect_project received a whole snapshot inventory and applied MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES before deciding whether a path was one of the manifest names it reads. An unrelated file therefore inherited a parser-specific limit.
resolution: Normalize every path, ignore non-manifest basenames before measuring content, and retain the same fail-closed size check for every actual stack manifest and iacode-quality.json.

prevention.description: A supported project containing an unrelated oversized policy file is still detected from its real manifest.
The same detector still refuses an oversized actual manifest and unsafe paths.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every parser-specific content limit applied to a broader inventory, prove unrelated content bypasses that limit while every interpreted candidate remains bounded.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A paired test with an oversized unrelated file accepted and an oversized interpreted file refused, plus a successful real repository evaluation.

provenance.notes: Derived from cmd-0044 against the committed Gate 4 stack; no external content was used.

notes: Path normalization remains inventory-wide because unsafe paths are a boundary concern; only the parser-specific byte limit is deferred until after candidate selection.

title: A polyglot plan binds each check to both its project root and its toolchain
symptom: After unrelated large files were ignored correctly, the real IACode snapshot was still refused because its Python plus Angular/TypeScript stacks had no exact single-stack policy profile.
rootCauseSummary: Detection collapsed a monorepo into a set of stacks but discarded which roots declared each stack, while execution chose one sandbox policy for the whole run. An exact composite profile alone would still have run commands from the repository root and reused the wrong image.
resolution: Preserve every detected stack/root pair in the content-addressed profile, add the exact closed composite policy, expand each policy runner at its matching roots, select sandbox policy from the frozen runner, and release sessions between checks so a run may change toolchains without changing ownership.

prevention.description: A Python and Angular/TypeScript monorepo produces checks at each declared root and common checks once at the repository root.
Python, Angular and common checks select only their policy-owned quality images from frozen runner identity.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every polyglot or multi-root project plan, prove each check is expanded at the roots that declared its stack and selects execution policy from the frozen runner rather than one run-wide guessed toolchain.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A deterministic planning test over multiple roots and stacks, an execution-boundary test for per-runner images, and a successful real polyglot repository evaluation.

provenance.notes: Derived from cmd-0049 against the committed Gate 4 stack; no external content was used.

notes: The policy still requires an exact declared stack combination; the change generalizes roots and toolchain selection without guessing a closest profile or accepting project-authored infrastructure.

title: Project discovery must separate deployable roots, nested fixtures and check applicability
symptom: The real IACode evaluation treated deliberately failing evaluator fixtures as independent projects and executed unit runners in packages that had no unit-test sources, producing failures unrelated to the committed repository's quality.
rootCauseSummary: The profile inventory classified every nested manifest as a deployable workspace root and the planner marked every profile runner applicable without preserving enough source inventory to decide whether a unit suite existed.
resolution: Preserve the bounded source-path inventory in the content-addressed profile, exclude fixture manifests from workspace-root discovery, and freeze unit checks as non-applicable and non-mandatory only when the corresponding root contains no test source.

prevention.description: A manifest below a fixtures directory remains test data and never expands the execution plan.
A source-only package records an explicit non-applicability reason instead of executing an empty suite.
The same rule cannot suppress a unit check when a test source exists.

applicability.requiredCheck: For project discovery over a monorepo, prove nested fixture manifests do not become execution roots and every non-applicable unit check is derived from the frozen source inventory rather than from a failed command.
applicability.requiredEvidence: Paired planner tests proving no-test roots are explicitly non-applicable, test-bearing roots remain mandatory, fixture manifests are excluded, and a real repository evaluation succeeds.

provenance.notes: Derived from cmd-0054 against the committed IACode snapshot; no external content was used.

notes: Non-applicability is limited to the absence of a recognisable unit-test source. A present suite remains mandatory even when it is expected to fail.

title: Every quality image must provision snapshots on its oldest runtime and prepare each isolated check
symptom: All Node checks failed before obtaining a sandbox because the shared helper called Python 3.12's tar extraction filter inside the Node image's Python 3.11, while successful provisioning would still have left later isolated checks without dependencies installed by an earlier sandbox.
rootCauseSummary: A shared helper was validated only on its newest interpreter, and the plan assumed dependency installation survived between checks even though toolchain changes intentionally release each sandbox session.
resolution: Replace version-specific bulk extraction with manually validated regular-file extraction supported by every pinned runtime, exercise snapshot provisioning in every real quality image, expose local Python packages through a policy-owned wrapper, and make every Node check bootstrap its pinned offline dependency cache.

prevention.description: Each pinned quality image provisions and reads an authorised snapshot through its actual helper runtime.
Closed Python and Node runners prove their per-check dependency preparation is part of the frozen command.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every shared helper and isolated quality runner, test the oldest pinned runtime actually used by an image and prove each check prepares all dependencies it needs without relying on a previous sandbox session.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A real snapshot-provisioning test across every quality image, closed-runner assertions for self-contained preparation, and a successful real polyglot repository evaluation.

provenance.notes: Derived from cmd-0054 against the real quality-node image and session lifecycle; no external content was used.

notes: The extractor retains path, link, type, duplicate-name and total-size checks; compatibility does not remove a security control.

title: Secret findings and reviewed false positives must share one policy-owned taxonomy
symptom: The repository's mandatory secret gate passed with reviewed digest-bound false positives, but the Quality Engine failed the same immutable snapshot because its three image-local scanners used a different broader pattern and had no policy-owned allowance mechanism.
rootCauseSummary: Secret detection logic was duplicated per image and diverged from the canonical finding kinds and allowlist semantics, so identical evidence received contradictory verdicts.
resolution: Use one offline scanner across all quality images, bind its canonical pattern taxonomy and reviewed digest allowlist into every content-addressed image, validate the policy structure fail-closed, and continue rejecting every matching value not explicitly allowed by policy.

prevention.description: Every quality image fingerprint includes the shared scanner and the canonical reviewed allowlist.
The shared scanner still fails an unreviewed credential-shaped value in every real quality image.

applicability.requiredCheck: Whenever more than one gate scans secrets, prove all scanners share the policy-owned finding taxonomy and digest-bound allowance source, and that an unallowlisted match remains blocking.
applicability.requiredEvidence: Content-addressing tests for scanner and policy inputs, a real negative scan in every execution image, and consistent PASS over the same reviewed repository snapshot.

provenance.notes: Derived from cmd-0054 comparison between mandatory repository scan and sandboxed Quality Engine scan; no external content was used.

notes: The evaluated project cannot add allowances through iacode-quality.json; allowances are image inputs owned by the service's canonical policy.

title: The canonical lint denominator must cover every detected project root
symptom: The mandatory lint gate reported PASS while the sandboxed Quality Engine found dozens of findings in the Model Gateway and Orchestrator rehearsal roots of the same committed snapshot.
rootCauseSummary: The lint command carried a manually curated root tuple that omitted two Python project areas, so its green verdict described only a subset of the repository profile detected by the Quality Engine.
resolution: Add every omitted source and test root to the canonical lint command, repair the real findings, and enforce that each non-fixture pyproject root intersects the lint denominator.

prevention.description: Every Python project root discovered from repository manifests is covered by at least one canonical lint root.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every manually scoped repository-wide quality command, derive or test its denominator against the current project inventory so a newly detected root cannot remain outside a green gate.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A denominator test over all non-fixture manifests plus a successful canonical lint execution and matching real repository Quality Engine verdict.

provenance.notes: Derived from cmd-0054 comparison of the mandatory lint gate and the same committed snapshot evaluated per detected root; no external content was used.

title: A failed verification stage must not leave an older PASS report addressable

applicability.requiredEvidence: A control that starts with a stale PASS file and observes it absent before the stage command is launched.

applicability.requiredEvidence: Lesson validation proving every evidence reference is a resolvable repository file and no lesson evidence path begins with file:var/.

title: Domain not-applicability and operational failure need distinct orchestration outcomes
symptom: The real sandbox-coding run completed all agent stages over a synthetic snapshot, then the post-run quality activity raised QUALITY_PLAN_FAILED because no supported project stack was detected. Temporal failed the workflow while the durable run row remained RUNNING.

title: Secret detection must run on the exact bytes at the durable evidence boundary
symptom: The independent G4-X7 attack sent a credential-shaped value under an ordinary structured key; normal mapping redaction left it intact and the Quality Engine persisted and resolved the serialized evidence.

prevention.description: A canonical synthetic marker under an ordinary key is refused with zero object and metadata writes.
The exact activity-to-store path terminates as sanitized ERROR and derives FAIL without retaining prohibited bytes.

applicability.requiredCheck: For every durable evidence boundary, scan the exact serialized bytes with the canonical taxonomy before lookup or write, fail closed when scanning cannot complete, and prove rejected bytes cannot resolve or support a verdict.
applicability.requiredEvidence: A direct zero-write persistence test, a scanner-failure test, a resolution test, and an end-to-end activity attack that derives a failing verdict.

title: Accepted cancellation must be enforced from durable state across activity boundaries

source.finding: cmd-0023, cmd-0060 and focused diagnostic cmd-0068

symptom: Two complete verifiers observed an accepted quality cancellation remain non-terminal for the full 900-second observation bound. The focused cmd-0068 reproduction proved the run was already CANCELLING when a racing sandbox response completed normally; persisting that success was correctly refused as late, and the workflow never reached terminal cancellation.
rootCauseSummary: The first guard covered one in-memory signal race after CHECK_DISPATCHED but not the whole accepted-cancellation state machine. A flag already set before activity-handle assignment could make the watcher exit without cancelling, and a normal response racing with persisted CANCELLING was recorded before cancellation precedence was applied. The store correctly refused that non-cancelled result, leaving the workflow failed and the run non-terminal.
resolution: Treat persisted CANCELLING as authoritative before creation and throughout the activity. Cancel immediately when the flag is already set, poll durable state while waiting, and normalize any normal response that races with accepted cancellation to CANCELLED before persistence; release the sandbox before the terminal transition. Cmd-0071 proved the complete path in a disposable real stack. CP0010 closes result and verdict persistence races with durable reconciliation and a cancellation/verdict commit barrier (ADR-0038).

prevention.description: The workflow re-reads durable run state after CHECK_DISPATCHED and before workflow.start_activity.
A CANCELLING run observed while an activity is in flight cancels that activity even without relying on the signal handler.
An already accepted signal cannot make the durable watcher exit while leaving the newly assigned activity running.
A normal activity response racing with accepted cancellation is persisted as CANCELLED, never as late success.
A database cancellation arriving after the durable read recovers from the rejected result callback, reaches CANCELLED and derives FAIL without a signal.
PostgreSQL serializes cancellation acceptance with immutable verdict commitment under the same run-row lock.

applicability.requiredCheck: When cancellation is accepted durably, the workflow must observe it before starting and while awaiting a long-running activity, cancel any newly assigned handle, give cancellation precedence over a racing normal response, and wait for cleanup before becoming terminal.
applicability.requiredEvidence: Deterministic dispatch, handle-handoff, in-flight durable-state and response-precedence regressions, the rebuilt evaluator suite, and a live checkout-owned cancellation scenario that reaches CANCELLED with cancellation evidence and cleanup.
